claims.text: Minor yttrium doping of CoCrFeNi will promote in situ formation of a stable oxide scale.
The yttrium-promoted oxide scale will be adherent and lubricious.
The proposed oxide scale will maintain low friction from room temperature to 800 °C.
The proposed oxide scale will maintain low wear from room temperature to 800 °C.
Yttrium will segregate at oxide grain boundaries in the modified CoCrFeNi alloy.
Yttrium segregation at grain boundaries will enhance oxide-scale adhesion and integrity.
Yttrium doping will modify the oxidation kinetics of CoCrFeNi.
Tribo-oxidation can produce a protective oxide glaze that provides solid lubrication during high-temperature sliding.
A dense, stable oxide layer can improve oxidation and tribological resistance at 800 °C.
The yttrium-promoted glaze will resist spallation during sliding.
The yttrium-promoted glaze will remain cohesively bonded under both low- and high-temperature sliding.
Yttrium-doped CoCrFeNi will have a consistently lower coefficient of friction than undoped CoCrFeNi throughout 25–800 °C.
Yttrium-doped CoCrFeNi will have a lower specific wear rate than undoped CoCrFeNi throughout 25–800 °C.
Unmodified CoCrFeNi suffers from unstable oxide formation and increased friction and wear at elevated temperatures.
Sliding tests are proposed in air from approximately 25 °C to 800 °C under a normal load of approximately 5–10 N.
Normal loads of approximately 5–10 N are typical of relevant tribological evaluations.
The optimal yttrium concentration and magnitude of tribological improvement may depend on processing conditions.
A controlled comparison of undoped and yttrium-doped CoCrFeNi using identical sliding conditions can test the hypothesis.
Failure to obtain statistically significant reductions in both friction coefficient and wear rate across the full temperature range would falsify the predicted performance.
